accepted.question_text: Let κ > ω₁ be a cardinal. Is it consistent with ZFC that every perfect generalized ordered space whose local density is at most κ has a σ-closed-discrete dense subset? Equivalently, is it consistent with ZFC that every perfect non-Archimedean space of local density at most κ is metrizable, and that every perfect generalized ordered space of local density at most κ with a point-countable base is metrizable?

evidence.quote: Question 1. Let κ > ω1 be a cardinal number. Is it consistent with ZFC that any perfect GO-space with local density ≤ κ must have a σ-closed-discrete dense set? Equivalently, is it consistent with ZFC that every perfect non-Archimedean space with local density ≤ κ is metrizable? Is it consistent with ZFC that every perfect GO-space with local density ≤ κ and with a point-countable base is metrizable?

accepted.question_text: Let κ > ω₁ be a cardinal. Is it consistent with ZFC that every perfect generalized ordered space X with local density at most κ embeds into some perfect linearly ordered topological space, without requiring the embedding to be monotone and without requiring the image h[X] to be open, closed, or dense in that perfect linearly ordered topological space?

evidence.quote: Question 2 (The GO-embedding problem). Let κ > ω1 be a cardinal number. Is it consistent with ZFC that every perfect GO-space X with local density ≤ κ embeds in some perfect LOTS? (Note: the embedding map h is not required to be monotonic and h[X] is not required to be open, or closed, or dense, in the perfect LOTS.)

accepted.question_text: Characterize the generalized ordered spaces that are cleavable over the class S of separable metrizable spaces, without imposing any additional restrictions on cardinal functions of the space.

evidence.quote: A space X is cleavable over M [1] if for each subset A ⊆ X, there is a continuous fA from X into some member of M such that fA (x) 6= fA (y) for each x ∈ A and y ∈ X \A. The property cleavable over S is analogously defined, where S is the class of all separable metrizable spaces.
Question 3. Characterize GO-spaces that are cleavable over S without imposing restrictions on the cardinal functions of X.

accepted.question_text: Characterize the generalized ordered spaces that are divisible by open sets, meaning that in the cleavability-style countable separating family, the sets used can always be chosen to be open, though not necessarily cozero-sets.

evidence.quote: (c) X is divisible by cozero sets, i.e., for each A ⊆ X, there is a countable collection CA of cozero subsets of X with the property that given x ∈ A and y ∈ X \ A, some C ∈ CA has x ∈ C ⊆ Y \ {y}.
Question 4. Characterize GO-spaces that are divisible by open sets (in which the collection C mentioned in (c) above consists of open sets, but not necessarily cozero-sets).

accepted.question_text: Characterize the generalized ordered spaces that are cleavable over the real line R; that is, characterize those GO-spaces for which the cleaving maps f_A can always be chosen to have codomain R.

evidence.quote: Question 5. Characterize GO spaces that are cleavable over R, i.e., in which the cleaving functions fA can always be taken to be mappings into R.

accepted.question_text: If a compact Hausdorff space X is cleavable over some linearly ordered topological space or, more generally, over some generalized ordered space L, must X itself be a linearly ordered topological space? Does the answer change if X is additionally assumed to be zero-dimensional?
accepted.context_brief: Cleavability of compact spaces over ordered spaces

evidence.quote: Question 6. Arhangelskii has asked whether a compact Hausdorff space X that is cleavable over some LOTS (or GO-space) L must itself be a LOTS. What if X is zero-dimensional?

accepted.question_text: If a compact Hausdorff space X is cleavable over an infinite homogeneous linearly ordered topological space L, must X embed into L?
accepted.context_brief: Embeddability after cleavability over homogeneous LOTS

evidence.quote: Question 7 (Buzyakova). Is a compact Hausdorff space X that is cleavable over an infinite homogeneous LOTS L must be embeddable in L?

accepted.question_text: A space is monotonically Lindelöf if every open cover U has a countable open refinement r(U) such that whenever U refines V, the chosen refinement r(U) refines r(V). In the class of generalized ordered spaces, is every perfect monotonically Lindelöf space separable, and is every hereditarily monotonically Lindelöf GO-space separable? In addition, if a Souslin line exists, is there a compact Souslin line that is hereditarily monotonically Lindelöf, and is there a Souslin line that is not monotonically Lindelöf?

evidence.quote: A topological space X is monotonically compact (resp., monotonically Lindelöf ) if for each open cover U it is possible to choose a finite (resp., countable) open refinement r(U) such that if U and V are any open covers of X with U refining V, then r(U) refines r(V).

Question 8. Is every every perfect monotonically Lindelöf GO-space separable? Is every hereditarily monotonically Lindelöf GO-space separable? If there is a Souslin line, is there a compact Souslin line that is hereditarily monotonically Lindelöf and is there is a Souslin line that is not monotonically Lindelöf ?

accepted.question_text: If Y is a subspace of a perfect monotonically Lindelöf generalized ordered space X, must Y itself be monotonically Lindelöf?

evidence.quote: Question 9. If Y is a subspace of a perfect monotonically Lindelöf GO-space X, must Y be monotonically Lindelöf ?

accepted.question_text: (a) Is the lexicographic product space [0,1] × {0,1} monotonically compact? (b) If X is a first-countable compact linearly ordered topological space, must X be monotonically Lindelöf? (c) If X is a first-countable monotonically compact linearly ordered topological space, must X be metrizable?
accepted.context_brief: Monotone compactness and Lindelöfness in LOTS

evidence.quote: Question 10. (a) Is the lexicographic product space X = [0, 1] × {0, 1} monotonically compact? (b) If X is a first-countable compact LOTS, is X monotonically Lindelöf ? (c) If X is a first-countable monotonically compact LOTS, is X metrizable?

accepted.question_text: For a generalized ordered space X, if the off-diagonal subspace X² \ Δ has a dense Lindelöf subspace, must X be separable? If X is a Souslin space, can X² \ Δ have a dense Lindelöf subspace?

evidence.quote: Question 11 ([6]). Is it true that a GO-space is separable if X 2 \ ∆ has a dense Lindelöf subspace? If X is a Souslin space, can X 2 \ ∆ have a dense Lindelöf subspace?

accepted.question_text: In ZFC, does there exist a non-metrizable Lindelöf linearly ordered topological space X such that the off-diagonal X² \ Δ is covered by a countable family of rectangular basic open sets {U_n × V_n : n < ω}?
accepted.context_brief: Countable rectangular covers off the diagonal

evidence.quote: Question 12. In ZFC, is there a non-metrizable, Lindelöf LOTS X that has a countable rectangular open cover {Un × Vn : n < ω} of X 2 \ ∆ (i.e., a collection of basic open sets in X with {Un × Vn : n < ω} = X 2 \ ∆)?

accepted.question_text: Suppose X is a linearly ordered topological space that is first-countable and hereditarily paracompact off the diagonal, meaning that X² \ Δ is hereditarily paracompact. Must X have a point-countable base? Is it possible for a Souslin space to be hereditarily paracompact off the diagonal?

evidence.quote: Question 13. Suppose X is a LOTS that is first-countable and hereditarily paracompact off of the diagonal (i.e., X 2 \ ∆ is hereditarily paracompact). Must X have a point-countable base? Is it possible that a Souslin space can be hereditarily paracompact off of the diagonal?

accepted.question_text: Let P_S be the subspace of the Sorgenfrey line consisting of the irrational numbers, which is known to be domain-representable as a Gδ-subspace of the Sorgenfrey line. Is this subspace P_S also representable by a Scott domain?

evidence.quote: Let PS be the set of irrational numbers topologized as a subspace of the Sorgenfrey line. It is known [8] that X is domain-representable, being a Gδ -subset of the Sorgenfrey line. In fact, the Sorgenfrey line is representable using a Scott domain [12].
Question 14. Is the Gδ subspace PS of S also Scott-domain-representable?

accepted.question_text: Suppose X is a generalized ordered space that is countably compact but not compact, and every compact subset of X is a metrizable Gδ-subspace of X. Must X have a base of countable order?

evidence.quote: Question 15 (Suggested by R. Buzyakova). Suppose X is a GO-space that is countably compact but not compact and that compact subset of X is a metrizable Gδ -subspace of X. Must X have a base of countable order [18]?

accepted.question_text: Is there an elementary-submodels proof of the generalized Hahn–Mazurkiewicz theorem stating that a topological space X is a continuous image of a compact connected linearly ordered topological space if and only if X is compact, connected, locally connected, and monotonically normal?

evidence.quote: Nikiel proves a generalized Hahn–Mazurkiewicz theorem, namely that a topological space X is a continuous image of a compact, connected LOTS if and only if X is compact, connected, locally connected, and monotonically normal.
Question 16. Is there an elementary submodels proof of the generalized Hahn–Mazurkiewicz theorem above?

accepted.question_text: A space X is weakly perfect if for each closed subset C of X there is a Gδ-subset D of X with D contained in C and with closure equal to C. If Y is a subspace of a weakly perfect generalized ordered space X, must Y also be weakly perfect?

evidence.quote: A space X is weakly perfect if for each closed subset C ⊆ X there is a Gδ -subset D of X with D ⊆ C = clX (D).
Question 17 ([3]). Suppose Y is a subspace of a weakly perfect GO-space X. Must Y be weakly perfect?

accepted.question_text: Suppose X is a Lindelöf generalized ordered space with a small diagonal and suppose further that X can be p-embedded into some linearly ordered topological space. Must X be metrizable?

evidence.quote: Question 18 ([4]). Suppose that X is a Lindelöf GO-space that has a small diagonal and that can be p-embedded in some LOTS. Must X be metrizable?

accepted.question_text: Let < be the usual order on ℝ. For which subsets X of ℝ does there exist a tree T together with linear orderings of the nodes of T such that no node of T contains an order-isomorphic copy of (X,<), while (X,<) itself is order-isomorphic to the branch space of T? In addition, which Fσδ-subsets of ℝ are order-isomorphic to the branch space of some countable tree?
accepted.context_brief: Representability as branch spaces of trees

evidence.quote: Question 19 ([13]). Let < be the usual ordering of R. For which subsets X ⊆ R is there a tree T and linear orderings of the nodes of T so that (a) no node of T contains an order isomorphic copy of (X, <), and (b) (X, <) is order isomorphic to the branch space of T ? (Both R and P are representable in this way, but Q is not.) Which Fσδ -subsets of R are order isomorphic to the branch space of some countable tree?

accepted.question_text: An Aronszajn line is a linearly ordered set of cardinality ω₁ that contains no copy of ω₁, no copy of the reverse of ω₁, and no order-isomorphic copy of any uncountable set of real numbers. Can an Aronszajn line be Lindelöf in its open-interval topology without containing a Souslin line? If an Aronszajn line has countable cellularity in its open-interval topology, must the Aronszajn tree from which the line arises contain a Souslin tree?

evidence.quote: An Aronszajn line is a linearly ordered set that has cardinality ω1 , contains no order-isomorphic copy of ω1 , no copy of ω1 with the reverse order, and no order isomorphic copy of an uncountable set of real numbers.

Question 20 ([14]). Can an Aronszajn line be Lindelöf in its open interval topology without containing a Souslin line? If an Aronszajn line has countable cellularity in its open interval topology, must the Aronszajn tree from which the line comes contain a Souslin tree?

accepted.question_text: Suppose X is a linearly ordered topological space with a σ-closed-discrete dense subset, and suppose there is a continuous map Ψ:(X² \ Δ) × X → ℝ such that for every pair of distinct points x and y in X, the real-valued function Ψ(x,y) separates x and y in the sense that Ψ(x,y)(x) ≠ Ψ(x,y)(y). Must X be metrizable?

evidence.quote: Question 21 (Gruenhage and Zenor). Suppose X is a LOTS with a σ-closeddiscrete dense set and a continuous function Ψ : (X 2 \ ∆) × X → R such that if x 6= y are points of X, then Ψ(x, y)(x) 6= Ψ(x, y)(y). (Note that this is weaker than the existence of a continuous separating family.) Must X be metrizable?
